_comment: Hand-tuned look and feel for BP_Ship_Vanguard. Applied by Tools/Assets/import_ship.py after the size-based values from the manifest, so everything here wins. Edit, then run the import again (editor closed).
_comment_no_nanite: Parts imported without Nanite. The cockpit interior flies with the camera; with Nanite its motion vectors were wrong in fast flight, temporal anti-aliasing smeared the dashboard and broke the displays' type up (sharp with r.Nanite 0, Tools/Shots/display_sharpness.json, 19. 9. 2026). 150 k triangles, no LODs needed.

pawn._comment_flight: SC-1a light fighter: thruster accelerations per direction in cm/s^2 (981 = 1 G), SCM / NAV top speeds in cm/s, rotational inertia in deg/s^2. G-Safe and ComStab use the C++ defaults.
pawn._comment_boost: SC-1b. Boost (Shift): manoeuvring thrusters (retro, strafe, up, down) and rotation multiplied, G-Safe suspended. Afterburner (Tab, SCM only): main thrust multiplied, speed limit = SCM x afterburner_speed_multiplier x speed limiter, own fuel tank.
pawn._comment_landing: SC-2a. Gear (N): the Meshy model's skids were fused into the hull; Tools/Blender/build_ai_ship.py cuts them out into SM_Ship_Vanguard_Gear, which rises gear_stow_travel_cm into the hull when stowed (the nose skid hangs 1.1 m under the belly, the main skids 0.55 m). The pads' soles are the bottom of the collision box, so gear_extension_cm is 0. Precision mode (gear down or P): SCM top speed x precision_speed_fraction, turning x precision_turn_scale.
pawn._comment_cockpit: The cockpit interior (Meshy 'Spaceship Cockpit', part SM_Ship_Vanguard_Interior, placed by Tools/Blender/fit_ship_interior.py) replaced the placeholder boxes on 18. 9. 2026; placeholder_cockpit stays in the code for ships without an interior.
pawn._comment_cockpit_light: Dark cockpit as in the Star Citizen reference: the displays' glow (components.cockpit_displays) does most of the lighting, a faint key light 80 cm ahead of the eye (250 cm reach) and a fainter fill above the head keep the dashboard's shape readable. At 12 / 5 cd the dashboard was flat grey; with none it is black (Tools/Shots.ps1 -Preset cockpit_light, 18. 9. 2026). Shadowless, 12 cm large; keep them under the canopy roof.

camera_boom._comment: Meshy Vanguard (18. 9. 2026): 14 m long but 11.4 m wide and 6.2 m tall with the gear. Picked from a side-by-side of chase distances (chase_zoom 1.0 / 1.25 / 1.5 / 1.75 x 1700 cm): at 1.6x the whole ship sits under the HUD gauges; closer, its nacelles filled the bottom of the screen.

cockpit_camera._comment: Pilot's eye (SOCKET_Cockpit in Vanguard_ai_build.json, from Tools/Blender/fit_ship_interior.py): 65 cm behind the side grips of the cockpit interior, 22+ cm under the canopy roof, with a clear view ahead. Framed like the Star Citizen reference (Docs/UI/Screenshot 2026-09-17 201854.png): dashboard top 8 degrees below the eye, the displays 14-25 degrees, the pilot ~1.5 m from the dashboard. The first interior had the eye at (305, 0, 156), 0.75 m from its dashboard and the displays at the bottom edge. 19. 9. 2026 (author: the figures on the displays too small from the seat): the eye 20 cm nearer the dashboard and 3 cm lower, the view tilted 3 degrees down (pawn cockpit_view_pitch_deg): the displays ~20 % larger, the whole dashboard including the lower centre screen in view, the view ahead kept (Tools/Shots/cockpit_readability.json compares it with the old eye). SOCKET_Cockpit in the recipe moved with it (test_flight_modes: the camera sits on the socket).

cockpit_displays._comment: The displays' glow on the cockpit around them (rect lights at the Display_* sockets, UCockpitDisplayComponent). state_rate_hz 5: the figures change five times a second, like a real instrument's readout. Temporal AA (TSR) blends a number that changes every few frames with the one before (two values over each other, 19. 9. 2026: pixel animation, responsive AA, translucency after TSR and TSR's anti-flicker settings did not stop it); held for ~200 ms it settles and reads sharp.

materials._comment: Meshy Vanguard: one texture set, re-baked onto the decimated model's own UVs by Tools/Blender/build_ai_ship.py (PBR master M_Ship_PBR), plus the nozzle discs, which the game makes glow with engine load (slot name contains Emissive). The nozzle discs are large, so they glow at 15 instead of the old model's 40 (white-hot while merely hovering).

MI_Ship_Vanguard_Hull._comment: Meshy's paint is very dark navy (base colour ~0.04 linear, the procedural Vanguard's was 0.34) and ~85 % metallic, so in the game it read as a black silhouette (Tools/Shots.ps1 -Preset ship_views, 18. 9. 2026); metallic alone made no visible difference. base_color_tint 3.2 lifts the paint to a dark blue-grey steel, metallic_scale 0.5 keeps some sheen (2.2 until 20. 9. 2026: with the sky light raised to 0.7 for fill, Tools/Shots/look_fill.json showed 3.2 is where the panels read in space instead of blending into a silhouette; 4.5 went chalky). 20. 9. 2026 (author: the ship is blurry up close in the chase camera): the micro detail layer of M_Ship_PBR (Tools/Assets/generate_detail_textures.py, triplanar in the ship's own space) carries the surface the AI paint cannot - its 4K over a 14 m hull is ~3 mm a pixel. detail_normal_strength 0 turns it off.
MI_Ship_Vanguard_Hull._comment_cavity: 20. 9. 2026: the hull read as one flat colour, because nothing in the bake said where the recesses are - the ORM's red channel is the emissive mask for the screens, not occlusion. Tools/Blender/bake_ship_ao.py bakes T_Ship_Vanguard_AO.png (occlusion shader at half a metre, so it is panel gaps and greebles, not a dirty ship) and M_Ship_PBR darkens the paint by it (cavity_strength) and sends it to the Ambient Occlusion output (ao_strength). wear_amount thins the paint to bare metal where the grunge is strongest and the surface is exposed; above ~0.3 it went blotchy rather than worn (Tools/Shots/hull_zones.json).

MI_Ship_Vanguard_Interior._comment: Cockpit interior, re-baked at 4K with more texture where the pilot looks; never_stream keeps the textures at full resolution, the cockpit is always right in front of the camera. Its displays are a separate slot (MI_Ship_Vanguard_Screens). base_color_tint 0.6: darker, as in the reference.

MI_Ship_Vanguard_Screens._comment: The cockpit displays: unlit, they show exactly what the game draws into them (UCockpitDisplayComponent sets ScreenTexture to its render target at run time; in the editor they stay black). Lit glass reflected the daylight sky and washed them out. Emissive 1.8: at 3 the white type bloomed and blurred.

MI_Ship_Vanguard_CanopyFrame._comment: Inside of the canopy frame (build_ai_ship.py canopy_frame): dark painted metal that catches a little light - at base colour 0.02, matt, the struts read as flat black bars across the view.
